The Balcony
10 PM. The garden side of the Malhotra mansion. A borrowed ladder, a sleeping guard, and an eighty-one-year-old woman in a shawl holding a torch.
Second balcony on the left. If you fall, I never met you. If you break anything, I never met you either.
I'm only here as a lookout. I want that on record. Also, Nani-ji, your samosas are incredible.
You climb. The balcony doors are open. She's sitting on the floor in an old Monarchs T-shirt, eyes red, surrounded by wedding catalogues.
How... NANI. Of course. Of course it's Nani.
You shouldn't be here. If anyone sees, he'll trade you tomorrow and he'll never let me leave this house again.
"I didn't climb a ladder to talk about trades."
Say why you came.
"Come with me. Tonight. We'll figure it out."
Run away together.
Kiss her.
No more words.
Then why did you climb it?
Because I can't stop thinking about a girl who jumped into my auto.
And go where? He'd find us by morning. And Sethi would take everything my father has. I can't run. I tried once. I ended up in your auto.
The city disappears. The catalogues, the debts, the date of the final. For a long moment there's only the sound of the sea.
...Okay. So that's a problem.
Three hundred crore. My father borrowed it from Sethi Steel to keep the team. The wedding cancels the debt. That's the whole deal.
Footsteps on the stairs. Voices. You flatten yourself against the wall behind the curtain.
It's Kunal, on the landing below, on his phone. He thinks the house is asleep.
Relax, Papa. Once the wedding paperwork is signed, the debt converts to shares. Fifty-one percent. The old man's out by Diwali. The team is ours.
Meera? She'll do what she's told. She always does.
It was never about the debt. The Sethis want the whole team. And Meera is the key.
